question: Which of the following allotropes of carbon conducts electricity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Graphite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Graphite** is a crystalline **allotrope of carbon** that is widely recognized for its ability to **conduct electricity**, which is an exception among non-metals.
 
• In the structure of graphite, each carbon atom is covalently bonded to **three other carbon atoms** in the same plane, creating a series of **hexagonal rings** arranged in layers.
 
• The carbon atoms in graphite undergo **sp2 hybridization**. This leaves **one valence electron** per carbon atom unbonded and "free" within the layers.
 
• These **delocalized electrons** are mobile and can move throughout the graphite sheet, allowing it to act as an efficient **electrical conductor**.
 
• Due to this property, graphite is extensively used in the production of **electrodes** in batteries and industrial **electrolysis** processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diamond**:

 
 
• It is another major **allotrope of carbon** where each atom is bonded to **four other carbon atoms** in a rigid **tetrahedral structure**.
 
• This involves **sp3 hybridization**, meaning all **four valence electrons** are tightly held in **covalent bonds**.
 
• Because there are **no free or delocalized electrons**, diamond acts as an **electrical insulator**.
 
 
 
• **Fullerenes (C60)**:
 
 
• Discovered in **1985**, these are spherical allotropes of carbon, often called **Buckminsterfullerene** or buckyballs.
 
• While they possess **pi-electron systems**, pure fullerenes are generally **insulators** or **semiconductors** under normal conditions rather than conductors.
 
 
 
• **Charcoal**:
 
 
• This is an **amorphous allotrope** of carbon obtained by the **destructive distillation** of wood.
 
• Unlike graphite, its structure is highly **disordered and porous**, which prevents the effective flow of electrons, making it a **poor conductor** of electricity.
 
 
 
• **Allotropy**:
 
 
• This is the phenomenon where a single chemical element exists in **multiple physical forms** that differ in their **atomic arrangement**.
 
• Other allotropes of carbon include **graphene**, **carbon nanotubes**, and **coke**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lubrication**: Beyond conductivity, the **weak Van der Waals forces** between the hexagonal layers of graphite allow them to slide over each other, making it an excellent **dry lubricant**.
 
• **Thermal Stability**: Graphite has a very high **melting point** (above **3600 degrees Celsius**), which allows it to be used in high-temperature **crucibles** and **nuclear reactors** as a **neutron moderator**.
 
• **Comparison**: While **diamond** is the **hardest known natural substance** due to its 3D bonding, **graphite** is soft and slippery due to its 2D layered bonding.
